summary: Petition seeking Review of the order dated 11.1.2024 passed by the Commission in Petition No. 391/GT/2020 with respect to truing up of tariff of Farakka Super Thermal Power Station, Stage-III (500 MW) for the period 2014-19. Petition No. 391/GT/2020 was filed by the Review Petitioner, NTPC Limited, for truing-up of tariff of Farakka Super Thermal Power Station, Stage-III (500 MW) for the period 2014-19, in accordance with the provisions of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2014 (in short 'the 2014 Tariff Regulations') and the Commission vide order dated 11.1.2024 (in short the ‘impugned order’) disposed of the said petition. Aggrieved by the impugned order dated 11.1.2024, the Review Petitioner has filed this Review Petition on the ground that there is an error apparent on the face of the record on the following issues: 2. The Commission, after hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner, ‘on admission’ on 4.4.2024, issued notice on ‘admissibility’ and directed the completion of pleadings in the matter. 3. The Review Petition was listed on 29.8.2024, and the Commission, as a last opportunity, permitted the Respondents to file their replies in the matter and accordingly, adjourned the matter. **4.** Though the Review Petition was listed on 8.10.2024 and 23.10.2024, the same could not be heard on account of the request of the Petitioner for adjournment and due 5. During the hearing on 28.11.2024, the learned counsel for the Review Petitioner circulated the note of arguments and made detailed oral submissions on the aforesaid issues. None appeared on behalf of the Respondents despite notice. The Commission Part-heard the matter, after permitting the Review Petitioner to file its notes/compilation. 6. During the hearing on 14.1.2025, the learned counsel for the Review Petitioner, after pointing out that none of the Respondents have filed replies in the matter, prayed that the Commission may reserve its orders, as arguments have been completed in the matter. 7. Accordingly, based on the submissions and the documents available on record, we proceed to examine the issues raised by the Review Petitioner, as stated in the subsequent paragraphs: 8. With regard to the capitalization of initial spares, the Commission in the impugned order dated 11.1.2024 observed as under: _In addition, the Petitioner is directed to take all necessary action against the concerned vendors for the delay in delivery of initial spares, including the recovery of LD and penalty, as applicable in terms of award, and furnish the same, along with supporting documents, at the time of truing up of tariff for the period 2019-24 and the same will be considered in accordance with law.”_ (b) The ‘other charges’ claimed by the Review Petitioner for Performance Incentive charged by the Coal company is as per Clause 3.12.1 of Fuel Supply Agreements signed between the Review Petitioner and the Coal companies, as per which the performance incentive is payable when the seller delivers coal in excess of 90% of the Annual Contracted Quantity (ACQ). The above fact has been noted by the Commission in Para 120 of the impugned order, but in Para _Order in Petition No.10/RP/2024 in Petition No.391/GT/2020 Page_ **_7_** _of_ **_11_** 13. We have examined the submissions of the Review Petitioner on the issues raised in items B and C above. As regards the calculation of ‘other charges’ and Weighted Average Price of Coal, the Commission in the impugned order has observed the following: _Order in Petition No.10/RP/2024 in Petition No.391/GT/2020 Page_ **_8_** _of_ **_11_** 15. It is evident from the above that the Commission, after detailed deliberations, had worked out and considered the weighted average price of coal and also rejected the claim of the Review Petitioner for consideration of the incentive given to the coal company for working capital. It is not the case of the Review Petitioner that there are errors in the calculation of the weighted average landed price of coal, but the Review Petitioner has only challenged the methodology adopted for the calculation of the weighted average landed price of coal. Similarly, the Commission, while considering the prayer of the Review Petitioner for the grant of water charges, had examined the claim of the Review Petitioner and observed in the impugned order, that it had not furnished the basis for revision of the water charges and also not provided the details of the apportionment of water quantity among Stage I & II and III. In our considered view, the Review Petitioner has sought to re-argue the case on its merits, which is not permissible in review. The Review Petition has a limited purpose and cannot be an appeal in disguise. It is a settled proposition of law as enunciated in terms of the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Parsion Devi v Sumitra Devi r(1997 8 SCC 715) that the review proceedings are not by way of an appeal and have to strictly confine to the scope and ambit of Order 47 Rule 1 of CPC 1908 and that the judgment may be open to review, inter alia, if there is a mistake or an error apparent on the face of the record. An error that is not self-evident and has to be detected through a process of reasoning can hardly be said to be an error apparent, requiring the court to exercise its power of review. These principles of review have also been enunciated by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in its judgment in Kamlesh Verma v. Mayawati and ors. (AIR 2006 SC 75). We, therefore, find no reason to allow the Review Petition on this count. Accordingly, we hold that the prayer of the Review Petitioner for review of the impugned order on these counts is not maintainable. 17. Review Petition No. 10/RP/2024 (in Petition No. 391/GT/2020) stands disposed of
